claim.statement: If regime seams start showing through organized labor, the first places to watch are South Pars and Assaluyeh contract-worker networks, Ahvaz steel workers, and oil-worker demonstrations in Tehran; these nodes repeatedly surface demands over contractors, wage arrears, benefits, and direct employment.
claim.subject: South Pars, Assaluyeh, and Ahvaz labor nodes

evidence.summary: Iran International reported oil contract workers protesting outside the presidential office and linked the action to unrest in South Pars, Assaluyeh, Ahvaz, Ilam, and electricity distribution workers.

claim.statement: The Isfahan-Yazd water-transfer corridor is a first-tier seam monitor because farmer protests have escalated from rallies to sabotage of pumping stations and pipeline infrastructure, rapidly creating a drinking-water emergency in Yazd.
claim.subject: Isfahan-Yazd water transfer corridor

evidence.summary: Iran International reported month-long Isfahan farmer protests, pipeline and pumping-station sabotage, a temporary Zayandeh-Rud release, and emergency tanker distribution in Yazd.

claim.statement: Currency and gold stress should be watched first through Tehran's Saadi Street, Shush neighborhood, mobile markets, Grand Bazaar, gold shops, and exchange queues, because merchant closures and street rallies have preceded broader protest spread to other cities.
claim.subject: Tehran bazaar and currency districts

evidence.summary: AP reported shopkeeper rallies in Saadi Street and Shush near the Grand Bazaar after the rial plunged, with similar rallies in Isfahan, Shiraz, and Mashhad.

claim.statement: Energy and fuel seams should be tracked through presidential admissions, Tavanir schedules, provincial closure notices, and unannounced power-cut complaints; official statements about shortages are likely to appear before protests when the state needs public cooperation to manage demand.
claim.subject: Iran energy and fuel administration

evidence.summary: Iran International reported President Pezeshkian acknowledging shortages including energy and fuel and warning that unrealistic promises would weaken public trust.

claim.statement: Internet measurement feeds are one of the earliest external signals of coercive state stress: IODA active probing, telescope traffic, BGP stability, Google product reachability, Cloudflare Radar, Kentik, and NetBlocks can reveal tiered or whitelisted access even when domestic reporting is suppressed.
claim.subject: Iran internet measurement feeds

evidence.summary: IODA reported active probing near 3%, evidence of tiered 'Internet Pro' access, and corroboration from Cloudflare Radar and Kentik.

claim.statement: Healthcare stress should be watched through nurses' protests in Mashhad and follow-on actions in Kermanshah, Yasouj, Tabriz, Ahvaz, and Sanandaj; demands over unpaid wages, allowances, workload, and staffing shortages expose public-service fragility before it becomes a wider hospital-collapse story.
claim.subject: Nurse protest networks

evidence.summary: IranWire reported a third day of Mashhad nurse strikes and similar protests in Kermanshah, Yasouj, Tabriz, Ahvaz, and Sanandaj over wage arrears and working conditions.

claim.statement: Retiree, teacher, and telecom-pension protests are useful low-noise seam monitors because they recur in named cities and outside identifiable offices, while their slogans often reveal whether economic anger is crossing into political blame.
claim.subject: retiree and teacher pension networks

evidence.summary: Iran International reported retiree protests in Zanjan, Tabriz, Tehran, Esfahan, Gilan, and Fars, including chants that blamed domestic authorities rather than foreign enemies.

claim.statement: Verified-video spread into Qom, Mashhad, Iranshahr, Kurdish-populated provinces, and other cities normally treated as loyal or peripheral is a high-salience seam signal because it shows protest geography crossing regime comfort zones.
claim.subject: province-level verified protest footage
claim.object: spread beyond Tehran and expected hotspots

evidence.summary: BBC Verify and BBC Persian reported verified footage in at least 17 provinces, more than 50 towns and cities, including Qom, Mashhad, and Iranshahr.

claim.statement: Qom is a legitimacy seam to watch less for protest size than for clerical-class fracture: non-official clerics and seminary students can carry public anger without receiving the privileges of the political clergy, while senior marja appeals expose distance between Qom's theological hierarchy and Tehran's ruling apparatus.
claim.subject: Qom clerical and seminary milieu

evidence.summary: The Week analyzed Qom protests as reflecting economic injustice among non-official clerics and seminary students and a rift between political clergy and Qom's traditional hierarchy.

assessment.uncertainty: Interpretive source; monitor with primary Persian clerical statements before elevating confidence.

claim.statement: Security-force pay delays, absences, and Artesh-IRGC friction are potentially decisive but highly contested seam indicators; they should be watched through multiple-source confirmation, visible deployment failures, funeral/casualty patterns, and refusals to attend pro-government rallies.
claim.subject: Iranian security-force morale and pay signals

evidence.summary: Iran International reported delayed Special Units salaries, unpaid army personnel, reported desertions, and affected deployments; the claims require corroboration.

assessment.uncertainty: Defection and desertion reporting is contested and may be vulnerable to information operations.

claim.statement: The No to Execution Tuesdays hunger-strike network is a recurring prison seam monitor because it reports weekly from named facilities, connects executions to communication restrictions, and can show whether repression is producing internal coordination instead of silence.
claim.subject: No to Execution Tuesdays prison campaign

evidence.summary: NCRI Women Committee reported week 116 of coordinated hunger strikes across 56 prisons amid internet shutdown and increased execution pressure.

assessment.uncertainty: Opposition-linked source; corroborate with HRANA, Amnesty, IHRNGO, family statements, and prison audio before high-confidence use.

claim.statement: Truck-driver strikes are a first-wave seam indicator because they can begin at Bandar Abbas and freight terminals, then propagate through privately owned heavy-vehicle networks into road, port, food, fuel, and industrial supply chains.
claim.subject: Iran truck-driver and freight network

evidence.summary: AP reported a truckers' strike beginning in Bandar Abbas, road and port blockages, fuel-price grievances, and public support from dissident figures.

claim.statement: Baker protests, card-reader returns, subsidy-payment delays, and bread-price warnings should be watched as household-staple seam signals because bread connects inflation, electricity cuts, subsidy systems, and daily food access.
claim.subject: Iran bakery and bread-subsidy system

evidence.summary: Iran International reported coordinated baker protests in Isfahan, Ahvaz, Birjand, Kermanshah, Qom, Shahinshahr, and Mashhad over costs, unpaid subsidies, and blackouts.

claim.statement: University reopenings, memorial gatherings, disciplinary text messages, Basij counter-rallies, and verified footage from Sharif, University of Tehran, Amirkabir, al-Zahra, Mashhad, and Isfahan are early indicators that suppressed protest energy is reappearing in organized youth spaces.
claim.subject: Iran university campuses

evidence.summary: BBC Verify reported confirmed footage of protests across eight Tehran universities plus Mashhad and Isfahan after campuses reopened.

claim.statement: Specific commercial districts are better seam monitors than generic 'bazaar' references: Shoush, Molavi, Grand Bazaar sections, Chaharsouq, Lalehzar, mobile-phone markets, gold markets, and Isfahan's Naghsh-e Jahan Square can show localized strike diffusion before national summaries catch up.
claim.subject: Iran commercial market districts

evidence.summary: Iran International reported Shoush and Molavi shop closures, Grand Bazaar gatherings, and Naghsh-e Jahan shopkeeper participation during currency-linked protests.

claim.statement: Shipping, insurance, AIS, and freight-rate data around Hormuz are external seam monitors for regime crisis behavior because maritime insurers, shipowners, and traffic trackers react quickly to credible threat, blockade, or state-control changes even when Tehran frames the issue politically.
claim.subject: Hormuz shipping and insurance market

evidence.summary: Reuters reported war-risk cancellations, damaged or stranded tankers, surging premiums, and a near halt in Hormuz traffic.

claim.statement: Steel, cement, aluminum, petrochemical, and automotive production cuts are economic seam monitors because power curtailment converts infrastructure shortage into wage delays, tax-account freezes, output collapse, and layoffs in strategically important industrial cities.
claim.subject: energy-intensive Iranian industries
claim.object: power-shortage transmission into layoffs and wage stress

evidence.summary: Iran International reported nearly all steel units shut down after severe electricity cuts, with delayed wages at Esfahan Steel and production impacts beyond steel.

claim.statement: Khuzestan wetland shrinkage, especially Hoor Al-Azim and Shadegan, is a physical-environment seam to watch because satellite-observed wetland loss correlates with more dust events and polluted days, turning water mismanagement into school closures, hospital strain, and local anger.
claim.subject: Khuzestan wetland and dust system
claim.object: environmental stress becoming public-health and protest stress

evidence.summary: Scientific Reports found strong inverse correlations between wetland area and dust-event frequency in Hoor Al-Azim and Shadegan using satellite data.

claim.statement: Tehran's water-pressure drops, rationing schedules, reservoir levels, pipe leakage, groundwater dependence, and land-subsidence damage are first-order state-capacity indicators because they affect the capital's residential towers, hospitals, emergency planning, and administrative core.
claim.subject: Tehran water and subsidence system

evidence.summary: Foreign Policy argued Tehran evacuation is infeasible, noted groundwater dependence, leaky pipes, edge-settlement water shortages, and public-health risks.

claim.statement: Hijab enforcement should be monitored through business and cultural-venue pressure rather than only street arrests: cafe seals, fines, event cancellations, permit threats, SIM-card controls, and raids reveal how the state tries to restore ideological control while avoiding another Mahsa Amini-style ignition point.
claim.subject: business-mediated hijab enforcement

evidence.summary: NPR reported Tehran cafe raids and closures for serving women without head coverings, with business owners describing cafes as free spaces and financial penalties as significant.

claim.statement: Hezbollah budget, salary, displacement-payment, rearming, and Iranian-adviser flows are proxy-seam monitors because they reveal whether Tehran still has the cash, logistics, and command bandwidth to maintain strategic depth while domestic services are strained.
claim.subject: Iran-Hezbollah funding and rearming channel
claim.object: external proxy capacity under domestic stress

evidence.summary: Reuters reported Hezbollah drawing on a roughly $50 million monthly budget, mostly from Iran, for fighter salaries and rearmament.

claim.statement: The practical limits of Chinese and Russian backing are external-rescue seam monitors: diplomatic condemnations without tangible military or financial support indicate Tehran may be more isolated than regime messaging implies.
claim.subject: China and Russia support for Iran

evidence.summary: Reuters reported Russia and China standing aside beyond condemnation and concern, constrained by their own strategic interests.

claim.statement: Border crossings such as Shalamcheh, Bashmaq, Parviz Khan, Tamarchin, Taftan, and Mirjaveh are seam monitors because closures or detours quickly affect food supplies, fuel and bitumen transit, local border livelihoods, and security-force exposure in peripheral provinces.
claim.subject: Iran border-crossing network

evidence.summary: Reuters reported the Shalamcheh crossing closing and reopening after airstrikes, noting its role in Iraqi imports of vegetables and other food supplies from Iran.

claim.statement: Professional emigration is a slow seam to watch through credential requests, nursing-council certificates, residency vacancies, student-abroad counts, and reports from doctors, nurses, engineers, and software developers; it drains the state's technical and service capacity before visible collapse.
claim.subject: Iran professional emigration signals

evidence.summary: BMC Nursing found strong professional, economic, social, and political push factors behind Iranian nurse emigration and noted rising official certificate requests.

claim.statement: Provincial shutdown notices are practical first-warning sources: governorates, crisis committees, schools, banks, universities, and office-closure announcements expose energy, gas, water, heat, cold, dust, and pollution stress before it is reframed as ordinary weather management.
claim.subject: Iran provincial closure notices

evidence.summary: Iran Front Page reported Tehran and 26 of 31 provinces shut down because of electricity and gas shortages, with offices, banks, and schools closed except emergency services.

question.text: Which labor nodes move first if conditions worsen: South Pars contract workers, Ahvaz steel, electricity distribution workers, truckers, bakers, or nurses?
question.resolution_criteria: Timestamped protest sequence across local union channels, HRANA/Hengaw/IranWire/IranIntl reporting, and verified video from named workplaces.

question.text: Do Zayandeh-Rud releases, Tehran rationing, or Khuzestan/Sistan dust-water crises produce the next visible water flashpoint?
question.resolution_criteria: Daily river/reservoir updates, governorate notices, tanker distribution, school closures, farmer gatherings, and verified sabotage or road-block reports.

question.text: Can security-force pay-delay, absence, casualty, or desertion claims be corroborated by deployment gaps, funeral data, internal notices, or multiple independent outlets?
question.resolution_criteria: Two independent non-derivative sources plus observable deployment or pay-administration evidence.

question.text: Which commercial districts act as the earliest repeaters when the rial or gold price moves: Saadi, Shoush, Molavi, Lalehzar, Chaharsouq, Grand Bazaar, or provincial bazaars?
question.resolution_criteria: District-level closure reports tied to FX/gold-price moves, with time ordering across Tehran and provincial cities.

question.text: Does Iran's tiered internet model expand from crisis response into normal governance, and which professions or institutions receive white-listed access first?
question.resolution_criteria: IODA/NetBlocks/Cloudflare/Kentik traces plus domestic reporting on Internet Pro, white SIM cards, profession-specific access, VPN arrests, and business losses.

question.text: Are school, bank, university, and office closures clustering by energy, water, air pollution, or security need, and which province announces first?
question.resolution_criteria: Daily scrape of governorate/ISNA/IRNA/local notices tagged by stated cause, province, exemptions, and duration.

question.text: Do proxy and external-backer signals show rescue, retrenchment, or hedging: Hezbollah salaries and rearming, Iraqi militia autonomy, China oil purchases, Russia diplomacy, or UN votes?
question.resolution_criteria: Reuters/AP/UN/treasury/shipping evidence plus Lebanese and Iraqi reporting on funding, salaries, arms, advisers, and political constraints.

question.text: Which border crossing disruptions quickly transmit into local livelihood stress: Shalamcheh, Bashmaq, Parviz Khan, Tamarchin, Taftan, Mirjaveh, or Chabahar road links?
question.resolution_criteria: Customs throughput, crossing closures, truck waits, food and fuel price movement, local protest reports, and security incidents.

question.text: Does business-mediated hijab enforcement produce localized backlash from cafes, cultural venues, wedding halls, influencers, or Tehran metro users?
question.resolution_criteria: Sealed-business counts, permit cancellations, fines, customer footage, and rights-group reports linked to specific districts and venues.

question.text: Which emigration proxy moves first under stress: nurse credential requests, physician residency vacancies, student visa flows, software developer job loss, or passport/airport demand?
question.resolution_criteria: Professional-council certificate counts, ministry workforce figures, visa/student statistics, airport/airline reporting, and sector-specific interviews.

synthesis.title: Where seams would show first: Iran watch map after 25 research passes
synthesis.summary: The strongest early-watch map is not one place; it is a set of observable surfaces. Watch labor-energy nodes (South Pars/Assaluyeh, Ahvaz steel, truckers, bakers, nurses), water and environment nodes (Isfahan-Yazd/Zayandeh-Rud, Tehran water pressure and subsidence, Khuzestan wetlands/dust), economic-market nodes (Saadi, Shoush, Molavi, Lalehzar, Grand Bazaar, gold/currency queues), coercion and legitimacy nodes (IODA/NetBlocks connectivity, Qom clerical class, security-force pay and absence claims, prisons/executions, hijab-linked business closures), and external-pressure nodes (Hormuz insurance/AIS/freight, Hezbollah salary/rearming flows, China/Russia hedging, border crossings). The 25 searches were selected from three 10-line candidate rounds: first broad institutional surfaces, then granular provinces/cities/organizations, then external or administrative traces that can be monitored even when domestic reporting is blocked.
synthesis.limitations: Several 2026 conflict-era claims depend on fast-moving reporting and some opposition-linked outlets. Treat the map as an early-warning surface list, not a settled forecast. Highest-confidence monitors are external measurement or market traces (IODA, Reuters shipping, AP/BBC verified reporting, peer-reviewed environmental data). Lowest-confidence but high-impact monitor is security-force desertion/pay-delay reporting.

operations.reason: New 25-pass watchpoint synthesis broadens the previous fissure overview into the requested seam-monitoring map.
